BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Overall position

The Seller’s package materially departs from Wattlebridge’s agreed negotiating position. We should reject the proposed “general regime” as a universal limitation framework. In particular, the Seller is attempting to collapse Fundamental/Title, Tax and IP matters into the general warranty limits, rely on blanket data-room disclosure and Buyer knowledge, and leave material Completion risks unresolved.

The fact that the Seller’s proposed 20% cap / AUD 4.8m matches a possible fallback does **not** clear it: that fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost for this draft, which has not been given.

## Key pushbacks

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer pushback / reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **General cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Maintain the starting position: **25% / AUD 6m** for general warranty claims. Do not accept the fallback without Amelia Frost’s written approval. |
| **Thresholds** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket | Replace with **AUD 5k de minimis**, **AUD 50k tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. The Seller’s thresholds would exclude or substantially reduce recovery for ordinary DD and warranty issues. |
| **General claims period** | 18 months | Require **24 months after Completion**. The 18-month period is an unapproved fallback only. |
| **Fundamental / Title claims** | Same general cap and time limit | Reject. Fundamental and Title claims need a separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and no general de minimis, basket or Buyer-knowledge limitation. |
| **Universal limitations** | Caps, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to “all Claims of any nature” | Delete this formulation. It must not override distinct Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant or specific-indemnity regimes. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be outside all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy provisions and non-reliance protections, to the maximum extent enforceable. |
| **Disclosure** | All data-room contents, public registers and statutory records are generally disclosed | Reject blanket deemed disclosure. Require **specific, fair disclosure** against the affected warranty, with enough detail to identify the nature, scope and likely consequences of the matter. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. |
| **Buyer knowledge** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room/public records | Delete. This is an impermissibly broad knowledge exclusion and duplicates the defective general-disclosure concept. It must never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Any narrowly negotiated knowledge qualifier should be considered only with appropriately named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, not constructive knowledge imputed from Buyer advisers or materials. |
| **Tax and IP** | “Settled” under the general regime | Do not accept this assertion. Tax and IP remain **open** and must be documented as separate, tailored regimes; do not assume either unlimited Seller liability or that the general warranty regime applies. |

## Transaction-specific issues

### 1. Bluefen consent — material Completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue / 30% of revenue, and the current record contains neither a final consent nor evidence that its conditions have been met.

**Pushback:**
- Make **effective Bluefen consent**, and evidence that every condition to it is satisfied, a Completion condition.
- Reject satisfaction merely by delivery of a consent document.
- Reject “reasonable endeavours” as the substantive answer to a material customer consent risk.
- Require the consent to be in form satisfactory to Buyer, effective at Completion, without adverse conditions unless Buyer expressly accepts them.

### 2. Riverlark debt and security — must be cleared at Completion

The disclosure confirms approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding and no final security discharge exists.

**Pushback:**
- Require an up-to-date payout figure before Completion.
- Pay the facility **directly from Completion funds**.
- Deliver effective releases/discharges of all Riverlark security at or before Completion.
- Do not accept a release “following Completion.” Any post-Completion release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval; neither should be assumed.
- Ensure the debt-free/cash-free funds flow actually reflects this treatment.

### 3. Employee Completion bonuses — funds-flow gap

DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, but they are absent from the draft funds flow. There is also no treatment of payroll tax, superannuation or other triggered on-costs.

**Pushback:**
- Require the AUD 420,000 and all triggered on-costs to be expressly addressed as a funds-flow line item, or borne by Seller.
- Obtain confirmation of the contractual employer, payment date, eligibility conditions, accounting treatment and all on-costs.
- Do not permit a silent Completion cost to remain outside the agreed price mechanics.

### 4. Ironquay IP — inadequate limited indemnity

The Seller seeks to retain an indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, while the materials say Project Materials transfer only upon cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but is not independent confirmation of non-payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is available.

**Pushback:**
- Broaden the specific IP indemnity beyond simply the SOW3 payment, while preserving the practical SOW3 cure path.
- Require evidence of cleared payment and/or a confirmatory assignment and release sufficient to establish ownership of the relevant Project Materials.
- Do not accept AUD 180,000 as independently verified, whether as a liability, price adjustment or cure amount, without supporting evidence.
- Preserve tailored IP warranty and indemnity protection; do not permit the general cap to silently displace it.

### 5. Export/privacy incident — preserve evidence, investigate, update

The disclosure appropriately does **not** establish a confirmed breach, harm, notification requirement or quantifiable loss. The Seller’s statement that it is “not expected to be material” is unsupported and should not be accepted as a conclusion.

**Pushback:**
- Require preservation of all relevant logs, files, emails, access records and investigation materials.
- Require ongoing investigation, prompt written updates and Buyer access/cooperation as appropriate.
- Do not concede that there has been a confirmed breach, loss, harm or notification obligation; equally, do not accept that there is none.
- Ensure disclosure and Buyer-review activity do not bar a later claim if the facts develop.

### 6. Sandbar renewals — no automatic classification

The AUD 330,000 renewals may be ordinary-course operating costs, but the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or otherwise relevant to Completion accounts.

**Pushback:**
- Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, payment/accrual status and approval history.
- Do not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct them from price.
- Reserve position pending the factual assessment.

### 7. Title — internal register is insufficient

DD-012 is an internal Company share register recording Harbourglass as holder of all issued shares. It is not independent proof of clean title, authority or absence of encumbrances.

**Pushback:**
- Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence, including appropriate corporate searches, PPSR searches, constitutional and board/shareholder approvals, share certificates/transfer documentation where applicable, and evidence of no third-party rights.
- Retain the separate Fundamental/Title warranty regime described above.
- Do not allow DD-012 or its disclosure to qualify title protection.

## Other disclosed matters to verify

- **Office lease:** Confirm the notification obligation, timing, consequences and whether any landlord response or consent is in fact required. Do not accept the Seller’s characterisation as determinative.
- **Mossvale:** Confirm the scope of the assignment restriction and whether any change-of-control, indirect-transfer or related restriction applies. Again, do not accept the Seller’s conclusion without reviewing the underlying provision.
- **Disclosure reservation:** The Seller’s non-admission wording is generally unsurprising, but cannot convert incomplete factual material into fair disclosure or shift the risk of undisclosed consequences to Buyer.

## Recommended negotiating response

1. Reject the Seller’s consolidated liability/limitations framework and mark up the SPA to preserve the Buyer’s separate general, Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity regimes.  
2. Reinstate the Buyer baseline: AUD 6m / 25% general cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, and 24-month general survival.  
3. Remove blanket disclosure, public-record and Buyer/adviser knowledge exclusions.  
4. Make Bluefen consent fully effective, with all conditions evidenced, before Completion.  
5. Require Riverlark payout from Completion proceeds and effective security releases at or before Completion.  
6. Resolve or expressly allocate the employee bonuses and all on-costs in the funds flow.  
7. Expand and evidence the Ironquay IP solution; preserve a tailored indemnity and cure process.  
8. Put evidence preservation, investigation and update obligations around DD-006 in the SPA/Completion deliverables.  
9. Keep Sandbar neutral pending diligence and obtain independent title evidence.
